requirements.text: Ambitious and Hungry: "Far and away the best prize that life offers is the chance to work hard at work worth doing." - Theodore Roosevelt. We screen for comparable experience and strong fundamentals, not exact tool matches. Equivalent technologies are welcome.

Problem Decomposition and Algorithmic Thinking: You can take a loosely defined problem, such as recovering a reliable process from messy action logs, decompose it into tractable sub-problems, reason carefully about edge cases, and arrive at an approach. You are comfortable reasoning from first principles about data structures, graph algorithms, approximation, indexing, and time and space complexity when algorithms must operate over millions of executions.

ML, DL Breadth: Strong working knowledge across representation learning, sequence modeling, clustering, structured prediction, information retrieval, generative modeling, and modern foundation-model adaptation. You have the judgment to recognize when a problem calls for a learned model, an algorithmic solution, an LLM-based system, or some combination of the three.

Cross-Domain Research Translation: You read research from adjacent areas including frontier AI, computer vision, language modelling, process mining, program synthesis, information retrieval, graph learning, and knowledge representation, and can judge whether it applies. You can identify the core idea inside a method, understand the assumptions that make it work, determine whether those assumptions hold in your setting, and adapt the idea into a working prototype.

Research Judgment: You can distinguish a difficult engineering problem from a research problem, design experiments that isolate the important variable, and abandon an elegant approach when the evidence suggests a simpler method works better.

Applied Foundation Model Systems: Hands-on experience building reliable systems with modern language or multimodal models, including retrieval, structured generation, evaluation, grounding, and model adaptation. You understand the failure modes that arise when model outputs are used to recover structured process knowledge from noisy evidence.

Python Proficiency: Strong software engineering in Python, experience with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, comfort with data processing at scale, and the ability to write clean, tested, production-quality code.
Communication: You can explain an algorithmic tradeoff to both a researcher and a product manager, and you write clear technical and design documents.

A strong research track record, demonstrated through publications in top-tier machine learning, artificial intelligence, reinforcement learning, natural language processing, computer vision, or data mining venues.
Experience translating research ideas from published work into production systems with measurable impact.
Process mining: event log analysis, process discovery algorithms, conformance checking, or variant analysis.
Information extraction from documents: NER, relation extraction, table extraction, or structured output generation from unstructured text.
Multimodal data processing: extracting signals from screen recordings, UI screenshots, or interaction traces alongside textual data.
Foundation-model adaptation, including supervised fine-tuning, LoRA, synthetic-data methods, distillation, reinforcement-learning-based post-training, and evaluation of resulting model behavior.
Retrieval design, embedding strategies, chunking, re-ranking, and grounding against source evidence.
LLM-as-Judge systems, rubric design, calibration against human labels, and knowing when automated evaluation is insufficient.
Getting hands-on experience with LLMs, RL, RLHF, RLAIF, post-training (SFT), evals, graders, synthetic data, model training and production ML systems.
Faithfulness verification, constrained generation, confidence calibration, and methods for reducing unsupported model outputs.
Guardrails, input and output validation, graceful degradation, and monitoring for drift in production.
